title: Daulat Khan Brings Babur Toward Guru Nanak

blocks.text: Daulat Khan reports the situation to Guru Nanak and explains that Babur wants an audience with him. The Guru does not rush toward imperial summons; instead he calmly directs the movement of the meeting on his own terms.

To prepare that encounter, Mardana is told to play the rabab so that music rather than force becomes the medium through which Babur and his people are drawn near. The page uses that moment to show that the Guru's court gathers itself through sound, serenity, and command rather than through royal ceremony.

Babur also asks what sort of offering should be brought before such a pir, and Daulat reminds him that spiritual and temporal authority alike rest with the Guru. The meeting is therefore framed not as a king honoring a subject, but as a ruler trying to understand the court before which his own power may have to bow.
